title: Salesloft pricing and reviews (2026)
summary: What Salesloft costs in 2026 after the Clari combination, its gated tiers and estimates, the Drift retirement, honest reviewer themes, and fit.
body_markdown:
Salesloft does not publish prices. Its plans (Essentials, Advanced, Premier) are quoted per deal on annual contracts, and third-party buyers put the Advanced tier at roughly $125 to $180/user/month. Since December 2025 it has been part of a Clari combination that adds forecasting. Reviewers praise the cadence engine and flag cost and complexity.


## Salesloft pricing at a glance (2026)


Plan


What it covers


Pricing


Essentials


Core cadences, email and call steps, basic reporting


Custom, contact sales


Advanced


Full engagement platform, Rhythm AI prioritization, analytics


Custom, contact sales (est. ~$125 to $180/user/month)


Premier


Advanced governance, coaching, deal and forecast depth (with Clari)


Custom, contact sales


Every figure is gated. The Advanced estimate comes from third-party buyer reports, not a published rate, and pricing is negotiated annually. The Clari combination means forecasting and revenue-intelligence capabilities increasingly sit alongside the engagement tiers, which can change how a deal is bundled and priced.


## How much does Salesloft cost in practice?


A seat rate is only the starting point. Salesloft sells annual contracts with seat minimums, so a team commits to a headcount-based spend up front. For a 25-seat team at the middle of the reported Advanced range, licenses alone run into the low six figures a year before anything else.


On top of licenses, budget for onboarding and an operations owner. Salesloft is a full platform, and reviewers report that the payoff depends on someone building and maintaining cadences, rulesets, and reporting. After the Clari combination, some buyers are also weighing forecasting and revenue-intelligence modules, which broaden the platform and the potential spend. In practice, a negotiated seat rate is the floor, and implementation, admin time, and any added modules determine the real cost per productive rep.


## What do the Salesloft tiers include?


Salesloft's tiers step up along cadence depth, AI prioritization, and governance. Essentials covers the core engagement job, cadences with email and call steps and basic reporting. Advanced is where most buyers land, and it adds the full platform, Rhythm (Salesloft's AI signal-to-action prioritization), and richer analytics. Premier layers on advanced governance, coaching, and deeper deal and forecast capability, which is where the Clari combination shows up most. For the software category, see[email sequencing software](https://www.artisan.co/blog/email-sequencing-software) .


The combination is the main change for buyers in 2026. Pairing Salesloft's cadence engine with Clari's forecasting gives revenue leaders engagement and pipeline visibility from one vendor. Reviewers see the logic. They also note that integrations, roadmap, and support can wobble in the year after a merger of this size, so new buyers should ask pointed questions about what is bundled today versus promised later.


## What are the hidden costs of Salesloft?


The usual suspects are annual lock-in, seat minimums, implementation, and negotiated pricing that varies by buyer. Because there is no public rate, comparable companies can pay different amounts, which rewards buyer bargaining power and makes clean budgeting harder.


There is also a stability question worth pricing in. Salesloft's former sibling product Drift suffered an OAuth breach in August 2025 that affected over 700 organizations, per Google Threat Intelligence reporting, and Drift's retirement was announced in March 2026, with clients referred to 1mind. This does not touch the Salesloft engagement product directly, but it is a reasonable prompt to review security posture and contractual continuity during the post-combination period. For a large team, the cost of a mid-contract platform change is real, so continuity is part of the total cost of ownership.


## What do reviewers say about Salesloft?


The consensus is that Salesloft is a mature, well-liked cadence platform that revenue teams trust for structured outbound and follow-up. Reviewers report that the cadence engine is intuitive, that Rhythm's signal prioritization helps reps work the right accounts first, and that the analytics and coaching tools support a disciplined sales motion. Usability tends to score better here than at some heavier enterprise platforms.


The criticisms track the category. Reviewers report that pricing is opaque and negotiated, that seat-based cost grows with headcount, and that the platform takes real configuration and admin effort to run well. Since the Clari combination, some note uncertainty around roadmap, support, and how forecasting is bundled. On balance, Salesloft is a strong engagement engine with a human-driven core, priced and administered like the enterprise platform it is. For the category and a close comparison, see[the best sales engagement platforms](https://www.artisan.co/blog/the-best-sales-engagement-platforms) and[Artisan vs. Gong Engage](https://www.artisan.co/blog/artisan-vs-gong-engage) .


## Who is Salesloft best for, and not for?


Salesloft best fits mid-market and enterprise revenue teams that want a proven cadence platform, value usability, and now expect engagement and forecasting from one vendor via the Clari combination. Teams with a revenue operations (RevOps) owner and reps who live in sequences see the most value from it.


It fits less well for small teams sensitive to annual seat commitments, and for buyers who want an AI to run outbound instead of a system that helps reps run it. Like every sales-engagement platform, Salesloft orchestrates people. The messages, calls, and replies still come from your reps. Buyers who are risk-averse about vendor transitions should also weigh the post-combination period before signing a long-term contract.

## FAQ


### How much does Salesloft cost per user?


Salesloft does not publish per-user pricing. Its Essentials, Advanced, and Premier plans are quoted per deal on annual contracts. Third-party buyers estimate the Advanced tier at roughly $125 to $180/user/month, before implementation and any Clari forecasting modules. Treat this as an estimate, not a published rate, until you have a quote.


### Is Salesloft owned by Clari now?


Salesloft's combination with Clari completed December 3, 2025, under post-merger CEO Steve Cox. It is a Vista Equity Partners-backed combination that pairs Salesloft's engagement platform with Clari's forecasting and revenue intelligence. For buyers, it means engagement and forecasting can come from one vendor, and it is reasonable to ask what is bundled today versus on the roadmap.


### What happened to Drift?


Drift, formerly a sibling product to Salesloft, suffered an OAuth breach in August 2025 that affected more than 700 organizations, per Google Threat Intelligence reporting. Drift's retirement was announced in March 2026, with clients referred to 1mind as the successor. This does not affect the Salesloft engagement product directly, but it is a fair prompt to review security and continuity.


### Is Salesloft worth it?


For mid-market and enterprise teams that run structured outbound and value usability, reviewers generally find Salesloft worth the price, especially now that forecasting is available through the Clari combination. For small teams or buyers who want AI to run outbound instead of helping reps run it, the annual seat commitment and admin overhead may outweigh the benefit. It depends on whether your constraint is rep efficiency or headcount.


### Does Salesloft have a free trial?


No public self-serve free trial. Access starts with a sales conversation and a demo, and pricing is negotiated per deal on an annual contract. Buyers who want to test software before an annual commitment should build this into the evaluation timeline and ask about pilot terms directly.


### What are alternatives to Salesloft?


Direct alternatives include Outreach (also gated, roughly $100 to $165/user/month by third-party estimates) and lighter sequencers like Klenty and Reply.io with published per-seat pricing. If the goal is fewer tools and an AI that runs outbound end to end instead of another seat-based cadence platform, Artisan uses a usage-based model with a free trial.
